purpose: Record applicability and evidence-backed verdicts for OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 chapter V10 (OAuth and OIDC) — 36 requirements — in the machine-readable decision register, with no code changes.
requiredInvariants: Every V10 requirement gets a decision: APPLICABLE with PASS/FAIL, or NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_JUSTIFICATION with a condition tied to a real, checkable absence in the tree; none is silently skipped.

A NOT_APPLICABLE verdict is only used where the artifact the requirement operates on (a token, an authorization-server endpoint, a consent surface) does not exist anywhere in the codebase, verified by grep against the live tree in this pass, not assumed from the feature being disabled by default.

The incompleteness of the one real OAuth/OIDC-shaped code path (the gov-id relying-party bridge — state checked, nonce generated but never validated, no token exchange) is named explicitly in the affected notes rather than hidden behind NOT_APPLICABLE.
A PASS (state-based CSRF protection) is only recorded where the enforcing code was re-read on the live tree in this pass.
No security control is weakened; Semgrep, the pinning ratchet and every other gate stay at full strength.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation.
This scope changes no application code.
acceptance: docs/security/asvs-applicability-decisions.json gains exactly 36 new V10.* decisions and no duplicates.
The evidence gate rejects 0 decisions; decisionsApplied increases by 36; finalPass stays false.
scripts/security/*.test.mjs stays 60/60 (JSON-only change, no script logic touched).
V10.2.1 is PASS with evidence naming the real state-generation and state-comparison code; V10.2.3 is FAIL with evidence naming the static, unvaried scope default.
Every NOT_APPLICABLE decision's condition is an ABSENT_IN_TREE check against real, verified-absent patterns, self-revoking if the situation ever changes.
